samples.xml_description:
<module id="multi_pipe_4bit">
    <description>Implement the design of 4bit unsigned number pipeline multiplier. It consists of two levels of registers to store intermediate values and control the multiplication process.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal. Defined as 0 for chip reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="mul_a">Input signal representing the multiplicand with a data width of <![CDATA[ <parameter refid="size"/>]]> bits.</input>
        <input id="mul_b">Input signal representing the multiplier with a data width of <![CDATA[ <parameter refid="size"/>]]> bits.</input>
        <output id="mul_out">Product output signal with a data width of 2*<![CDATA[ <parameter refid="size"/>]]> bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="size" value="4"/>
    </parameter_description>
    <implementation>Multiplication operation:
This operation must be constructed as combinational logic block.
The module uses a generate block to perform multiplication for each bit position of the multiplier (mul_b) and generate number of (<![CDATA[ <parameter refid="size"/>]]>) partial products. Each partial product is (2*<![CDATA[ <parameter refid="size"/>]]>) bit width.
For each bit position i from 0 to <![CDATA[ <parameter refid="size"/>]]>-1, each partial product is calculated as follows:
If the corresponding bit in the multiplier is 1, the corresponding partial product equals to result of (mul_a) left-shifted by i positions.
If the corresponding bit in the multiplier is 0, the partial product is set to 0 ('d0).
Add of partial products:
The module uses number of (<![CDATA[ <parameter refid="size"/>]]>/2) registers to store the intermediate sum values. Each register is (2*<![CDATA[ <parameter refid="size"/>]]>) bit width.
On the positive edge of the clock signal (clk) or the falling edge of the reset signal (rst_n), the module performs add operations.
If the reset signal (rst_n) is low, indicating a reset condition, the registers are set to 0.
If the reset signal (rst_n) is high, the registers are updated with the sum of the 2 corresponding partial products.
Final product calculation:
On the positive edge of the clock signal (clk) or the falling edge of the reset signal (rst_n), the module calculates the final product.
If the reset signal (rst_n) is low, indicating a reset condition, the product output (mul_out) is set to 0.
If the reset signal (rst_n) is high, the product output (mul_out) is directly updated with the sum of registers. The (mul_out) must not be updated though any middle sequencial logic value, but directly through sum of registers.
Testbench notice:
This module is under functional test of a testbench.
Af the clock (clk) cycle of latching inputs (mul_a) and (mul_b) for calculating multiplication, the testbench then check the multiplication result (mul_out) after that 1 clock (clk) cycle.
So, to pass the testbench, the (mul_out) must be designed to be asserted after 1 clock (clk) cycle of calculating multiplication of (mul_a) and (mul_b.)
You just need to notice this testbench operation and you don't provide the testbench code, but the module code only.
</implementation>
</module>
